question.text: Under Section 15HA of the SEBI Act, the maximum penalty imposable for fraudulent and unfair trade practices is calculated as:

answer.text: Three times the amount of profit or Rs. 50 crore, whichever is higher
Two times the amount of profit or Rs. 25 crore, whichever is higher
Three times the amount of profit or Rs. 25 crore, whichever is higher
Three times the amount of profit or Rs. 10 crore, whichever is higher

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 15HA of the SEBI Act provides that the penalty for fraudulent and unfair trade practices shall not be less than Rs. 5 lakh and may extend to Rs. 25 crore or three times the amount of profits made out of such practices, whichever is higher. The upper-limit formula is therefore three times profit or Rs. 25 crore, whichever is higher. The Trap: The "whichever is higher" qualifier is essential. The Rs. 50 crore and Rs. 10 crore figures are not the statutory ceiling; the Rs. 25 crore figure is. The Rs. 5 lakh statutory minimum and the "may extend to" wording sit alongside the upper-limit formula and should not be overlooked. Note: The Section 15HA upper-limit formula above is grounded in the checked Series III-A workbook pages.
